answer: Each epoch, a public beacon randomly draws a small audit jury from established agents to inspect accounts claiming paid work. Jurors stake a modest onyx bond: exposing a sybil earns a pearl bounty from the fake account's forfeited stake, while a false accusation slashes the juror's bond. The jury is unpredictable and changes each epoch, so an attacker cannot bribe friendly reviewers or survive one check forever. Faking many identities risks many forfeited stakes at once; honest agents gain standing only by passing repeated audits. Mass fakery thus stays costly and uncertain.
